- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–1.5% to capture mean reversion.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; apply a 2–3% downward correction in subsequent forecasts.  
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >5% deviation) and sentiment is neutral or mixed, assume lagged reaction; delay upward adjustment by 1–2 periods.  
- When sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-period, model often fails to adjust quickly; apply a 1–2% upward bias in the next 2–3 periods.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent volatility; smooth out extreme swings by applying a 1–2% dampening factor if sentiment is volatile or mixed.
